properties.name: Africa plate
properties.motion: north-east, about 2 cm a year
properties.note: Most of Africa (the Nubian plate). East Africa is splitting away along the East African Rift.

properties.name: Amur plate
properties.motion: slowly east
properties.note: North-east China, Korea and part of Japan; it may be pulling away from Eurasia along the Baikal Rift.

properties.name: Antarctica plate
properties.motion: hardly at all (about 1 cm a year)
properties.note: Antarctica and the ocean floor around it, ringed almost entirely by spreading ridges.

properties.name: Arabia plate
properties.motion: north-north-east, about 2–3 cm a year
properties.note: It split from Africa along the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, and pushes into Asia at the Zagros Mountains.

properties.name: Australia plate
properties.motion: north-north-east, about 7 cm a year (one of the fastest)
properties.note: Australia, New Guinea and the ocean around them. With the India plate it was once counted as one Indo-Australian plate.

properties.name: Caribbean plate
properties.motion: east, about 1–2 cm a year
properties.note: Most of the Caribbean Sea and Central America south of Guatemala.

properties.name: Cocos plate
properties.motion: north-east, about 8 cm a year (one of the fastest)
properties.note: It dives under Central America in the Middle America Trench, feeding its volcanoes.

properties.name: Eurasia plate
properties.motion: slowly east, about 1–2 cm a year
properties.note: Europe and most of Asia. Its collision with India and Africa raised the Himalayas and the Alps.

properties.name: India plate
properties.motion: north, about 5 cm a year
properties.note: India's collision with Asia, which began about 50 million years ago, is still raising the Himalayas.

properties.name: Juan de Fuca plate
properties.motion: east-north-east, about 3–4 cm a year, under North America
properties.note: A small remnant of the old Farallon plate, sinking under the Pacific Northwest in the Cascadia subduction zone.

properties.name: North America plate
properties.motion: west to south-west, about 2 cm a year
properties.note: North America, Greenland, half of Iceland, and part of Siberia and Japan.

properties.name: Nazca plate
properties.motion: east, about 5–7 cm a year, under South America
properties.note: Named after the Nazca region of Peru. It sinks under South America in the Peru–Chile Trench.

properties.name: Okhotsk plate
properties.motion: slowly
properties.note: The Sea of Okhotsk, Kamchatka and northern Japan (some count it as part of North America).

properties.name: Pacific plate
properties.motion: north-west, about 7–10 cm a year (one of the fastest)
properties.note: The largest plate, almost all ocean floor. Its edges make most of the Ring of Fire.

properties.name: Philippine Sea plate
properties.motion: north-west, several centimetres a year
properties.note: Almost all ocean. The Pacific plate dives under its east side in the Mariana Trench.

properties.name: South America plate
properties.motion: west, a few centimetres a year
properties.note: South America and the western South Atlantic. The Nazca plate dives under its west coast, raising the Andes.

properties.name: Scotia plate
properties.motion: slowly
properties.note: Between South America and Antarctica, bordered by the Scotia Arc of islands.

properties.name: Somalia plate
properties.motion: separating from Africa at a few millimetres a year
properties.note: East Africa and the western Indian Ocean, slowly pulling away from the rest of Africa along the East African Rift.

properties.name: Sunda plate
properties.motion: slowly east
properties.note: South-East Asia: Indochina, Malaysia, Sumatra, Java and Borneo.

properties.name: Yangtze plate
properties.motion: slowly east
properties.note: Southern China, between the Tibetan Plateau and the East China Sea.
